# Purplefish Agent

[![Test](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/purplefish-ai/agent/actions/workflows/test.yml)

This is our livekit based phone agent.

## Development

### Setup

1. Install the 1Password CLI: https://developer.1password.com/docs/cli/get-started/
2. Install uv: `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`
3. Install dependencies: `uv sync`
4. Install git hooks:
   ```bash
   # Install pre-commit hooks (runs on commit)
   pre-commit install

   # Install pre-push hooks (runs simulation tests on push)
   pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push

   # Or install both at once
   pre-commit install && pre-commit install --hook-type pre-push
   ```
5. Create local dev keys in Livekit
   1. Login to livekit, enter the `Local Dev <Your Name>` project (Martin will create this for you)
   2. go into Settings > Keys
   3. Create 1 new API Key
   4. Update the .env file to set the new API keys and Secrets. For local dev, we can use the same API key for all of these secrets.
      1. Set the API key to the values LIVEKIT_API_KEY_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_KEY_OUTBOUND
      2. Set the secret key to the values LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_OUTBOUND
      3. Set the Websocket URL to the values LIVEKIT_URL_INBOUND, LIVEKIT_URL_OUTBOUND
6. Download the model files for livekit `make download-files`
7. Run the agent: `make dev`

## Testing the agent locally using the livekit playground
1. Find the profile you wish to test and copy the profile id
2. Paste the profile id into the default value for the `PLAYGROUND_PROFILE_ID` env var in `env.ts` on the *MONOREPO* (not in the agent repo)
3. Connect to the livekit agent playground by visiting this URL: https://agents-playground.livekit.io/
4. Select your local dev env
5. This will launch a new interview locally.

## Testing Tools

### Simulation Mode
Simulation mode allows you to run automated conversations between the agent and an AI-powered candidate using real job IDs.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Basic simulation
make simulate <job_id>

# With custom parameters
make simulate <job_id> max_turns=30
make simulate <job_id> instructions="You are an experienced candidate"
```

The simulation will:
- Fetch real job and profile data from your development server
- Run an automated conversation with an AI candidate (GPT-4)
- Display color-coded conversation transcript
- Provide evaluation of interview completion

### Interactive Chat Mode
Chat mode lets you interact directly with the agent as a candidate through text input.

**Usage:**
```bash
# Start interactive chat
make chat <job_id>
```

Features:
- Real-time text interaction with the agent
- You play the role of the candidate
- No turn limits - chat as long as you want
- Type 'exit', 'quit', 'bye', or 'goodbye' to end
- Color-coded output (your messages in green, agent in cyan)

Both modes create a room name in format `demo:{job_id}_{unique_id}` and use the real job data from your system.

## Debugging
If you need to run the agent through your IDE so that you can debug, here's how to do it
- Entrypoint should be the `agent` script. The agent script will be in your uv virtual environment at `.venv/bin/agent`
- Run the script with the param `start`
- You might need to configure your IDE to write secrets to a file before you launch. Here's an example command you can use for that: `inject -f -i ./envs/.env -o ./envs/local`

## Running lints and checks locally

### Pre-commit hooks
After making changes locally, you can manually run the hooks:
```bash
# Run all pre-commit hooks on all files
pre-commit run --all-files

# Run specific hook
pre-commit run ty --all-files
pre-commit run pyright --all-files
pre-commit run ruff-check --all-files

# Type checking - dual system for speed and accuracy
make ty-check     # Fast (10-20x faster), Rust-based, pre-alpha
make pyright      # Comprehensive, mature, production-ready (source only)
# Note: Both type checkers run in make check
```

### Pre-push hooks
To manually run pre-push checks:
```bash
# Run simulation tests (same as what happens on git push)
make run-simulation

# Or run pre-push hooks manually
pre-commit run --hook-stage pre-push
```

This will let you catch lint issues and test failures before committing/pushing.

## Running the LiveKit CLI

We have a wrapper around the LiveKit CLI that respects the .env file.

First, install the LiveKit CLI with `brew install livekit-cli`

Run the LiveKit CLI with `uv run livekit <args...>`

## Testing

The project separates unit tests from simulation tests for better organization and faster CI/CD.

### Unit Tests

To run unit tests (excluding simulation tests):
```bash
# Run all unit tests in parallel
make test

# Run a specific test file or test
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py
make test path=tests/unit/test_example.py::test_specific_function
```

Unit tests are run in parallel using pytest-xdist for faster execution and automatically exclude any simulation test directories.

### Simulation Tests

To run simulation tests (integration tests that simulate full conversations):
```bash
# Run all simulation tests
make run-simulation
```

Simulation tests:
- Run with retry logic (3 attempts with 1 second delay)
- Stop on first failure for easier debugging
- Test end-to-end agent behavior with simulated conversations
- **Note**: Simulation tests run automatically during `git push` via pre-push hook. To bypass this check, use `git push --no-verify`

### Code Coverage

We use pytest-cov to track code coverage. Coverage reports are automatically generated in CI/CD for all PRs.

**Running tests with coverage locally:**
```bash
# Run all tests with coverage
make test-cov

# Run specific test with coverage
make test-cov path=tests/unit/test_example.py

# Check coverage summary
uv run python scripts/check_coverage.py
```

**Coverage outputs:**
- **Terminal**: Coverage summary shown after tests complete
- **HTML Report**: Open `htmlcov/index.html` in your browser for detailed line-by-line coverage
- **XML Report**: `coverage.xml` for CI/CD integration

**Coverage in Pull Requests:**
- Coverage reports are automatically posted as PR comments (free, no external service required)
- Lines missing coverage are annotated in the PR diff
- Visual indicators: 🟢 85%+ | 🟡 70-84% | 🔴 <70%
- Coverage summary available in GitHub Actions job summary
- HTML coverage reports uploaded as artifacts for detailed analysis

**Current coverage targets:**
- Overall project: 70% minimum (aiming for 80%+)
- New code in PRs: 80% minimum

To get a more end-to-end-test, run purplefish-ai/app with inngest (`npm run inngest`). After the call, from the app
folder, run `npm run send-end-of-room-event` to trigger all of the end of room logic, including sending emails and SMS.

## Voice Agent v4

Voice Agent v4 introduces a new architecture with modular task-based agents. The foundation includes:
- **Task Orchestrator**: Manages conversation flow through defined tasks
- **Specialized Agents**: Greeter, DataCollection, Information, and Closer agents for different conversation phases
- **Dynamic Tool Factory**: Creates conversation tools based on script configuration
- **Conversation Context**: Maintains state and data points throughout the call
- **Script-Driven Architecture**: JSON-based call scripts define agent behavior and conversation flow

### Running Voice Agent v4 Locally

To test the new Voice Agent v4 with the local development command:

```bash
# Run with 1Password for environment variables and uv
op run --env-file="envs/development.env" -- uv run screening_agent_local_dev --call-script-path examples/it_support_call_script.json
```

For all local_dev options run
```bash
op run --env-file="envs/development.env" -- uv run screening_agent_local_dev --help
```

This command:
- Uses 1Password CLI to load environment variables from `envs/development.env`
- Runs the voice agent v4 local development mode
- Loads the example IT support call script for testing

## Docker Build and Run Guide

This guide explains how to build and run the Purplefish AI voice agent Docker image locally.

### Prerequisites

- Docker installed on your system
- 1Password CLI configured (for production deployment)
- Environment variables configured

### Building the Docker Image

Build the Docker image with:

```bash
docker build -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

For a specific Python version:

```bash
docker build --build-arg PYTHON_VERSION=3.11 -t purplefish-agent:latest .
```

### Running the Docker Container

#### Development Mode (Local Testing)

For local development without 1Password integration, run with environment variables. See `envs/production.env` for the required variables:

```bash
# Set environment to bypass 1Password injection
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  -e VARIABLE_NAME="value" \
  # ... add all variables from envs/production.env ... \
  # can also pass in --env-file ./.env \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Production Mode (with 1Password)

For production deployment with 1Password service account:

```bash
docker run -it --rm \
  -e OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN="your-1password-service-account-token" \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Production \
  purplefish-agent:latest
```

#### Docker Command

By default, the container runs with `agent start` command

To run a different command (clarify in pyproject.toml project.scripts)

```bash
# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest screening_agent_local_dev --call-script-path "..." --no-simulate-room

# Generate development room token
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest generate_dev_room_token

# download livekit plugin
docker run -it --rm \
  -e AGENT_ENV=Development \
  # ... environment variables from envs/production.env ... \
  purplefish-agent:latest download_livekit_plugin_model
```

### Environment Variables

The container requires environment variables defined in `envs/production.env`. When running locally without 1Password:

- Set `AGENT_ENV=Development` to bypass 1Password injection
- Provide actual values for all variables listed in `envs/production.env`

For production with 1Password:
- Set `AGENT_ENV=Production`
- Provide `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` for 1Password service account access

### How It Works

1. The Dockerfile creates a lightweight Python 3.11 image
2. Installs system dependencies and required tools (1Password CLI, uv)
3. Creates a non-root user for security
4. Installs Python dependencies and downloads LiveKit plugin models
5. Uses `docker_entrypoint.sh` to handle environment setup:
   - In Production mode: Injects secrets from 1Password
   - In other modes: Uses passed environment variables
6. Runs the agent with DataDog tracing enabled

### Troubleshooting

- **Missing environment variables**: Ensure all required variables are set when not using 1Password
- **1Password errors**: Verify your service account token is valid and has access to required secrets
- **Model download issues**: The container pre-downloads LiveKit plugin models during build
- **Permission errors**: The container runs as non-root user `appuser` for security

## Versioning and Releases

This project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and [python-semantic-release](https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/) for version management.

### Commit Message Convention
We follow the [Conventional Commits specification](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/):

- `feat:` New feature (minor version bump)
- `fix:` Bug fix (patch version bump)
- `docs:` Documentation changes (no version bump)
- `style:` Code style changes (no version bump)
- `refactor:` Code refactoring (no version bump)
- `perf:` Performance improvements (patch version bump)
- `test:` Test changes (no version bump)
- `chore:` Build process or auxiliary tool changes (no version bump)
- `BREAKING CHANGE:` or `!` after type (major version bump)

Examples:
```
feat: add voice agent v4 support
fix: resolve timeout issue in call controller
feat!: redesign agent manager API
```

### Manual Release Process

To create a new release:

```bash
# Check what version will be released (dry run)
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create a new version (updates version in pyproject.toml, creates git tag, updates CHANGELOG.md)
uv run semantic-release version

# Push the changes and tags to trigger GitHub release
git push --follow-tags origin main

# Optionally publish to GitHub releases
uv run semantic-release publish
```

The release process will:
1. Analyze commits since last release
2. Determine version bump based on commit types
3. Update version in `pyproject.toml`
4. Generate/update `CHANGELOG.md`
5. Create git tag with version
6. Create GitHub release with changelog

   ```bash

   ```

    required: true

    description: "Whether a new PR was created"

    description: "The version for the release"
    value: ${{ steps.get-version.outputs.new_version }}
  pr-number:
    description: "The PR number if created"

      with:
        python-version: ${{ inputs.python-version }}

      uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
      with:
        enable-cache: true

    - name: Install dependencies
      shell: bash
      run: uv sync

    - name: Check for existing release PR
      id: check-pr
      shell: bash
      env:
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ inputs.github-token }}
      run: |
        # Find existing open release PRs
        EXISTING_PR=$(gh pr list --label "release" --state open --json number,headRefName --jq '.[0]')

        if [ -n "$EXISTING_PR" ] && [ "$EXISTING_PR" != "null" ]; then
          PR_NUMBER=$(echo $EXISTING_PR | jq -r '.number')
          BRANCH_NAME=$(echo $EXISTING_PR | jq -r '.headRefName')

          echo "Found existing release PR #$PR_NUMBER on branch $BRANCH_NAME"
          echo "existing_pr=$PR_NUMBER" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "existing_branch=$BRANCH_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          # Close the existing PR
          gh pr close $PR_NUMBER --comment "Closing in favor of new release PR"

          # Delete the branch
          git push origin --delete $BRANCH_NAME || true
        else
          echo "No existing release PR found"
          echo "existing_pr=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
        fi

    - name: Get next version
      id: get-version
      shell: bash
      run: |
        # Run semantic-release in dry-run mode to get the next version
        NEXT_VERSION=$(uv run semantic-release version --print) || true

        if [ -z "$NEXT_VERSION" ] || [ "$NEXT_VERSION" = "No release will be made." ]; then
          echo "No new release needed"
          echo "new_version=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          exit 0

      shell: bash

        VERSION=${{ steps.get-version.outputs.new_version }}

        PR_URL=$(gh pr create \
          --base main \
          --head ${{ env.branch_name }} \

           - Create git tag v$VERSION
           - Create GitHub release

        ---
        *This PR was automatically generated by the release workflow.*" \
          --label "release" \
          --label "automated")

        # Extract PR number from URL
        PR_NUMBER=$(echo "$PR_URL" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$')

        echo "✅ Created release PR #$PR_NUMBER for v$VERSION"

## Versioning and Releases

This project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/) and an automated release workflow powered by [python-semantic-release](https://python-semantic-release.readthedocs.io/).

### Commit Message Convention
We follow the [Conventional Commits specification](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) to automatically determine version bumps:

- `feat:` New feature (minor version bump)
- `fix:` Bug fix (patch version bump)
- `docs:` Documentation changes (no version bump)
- `style:` Code style changes (no version bump)
- `refactor:` Code refactoring (no version bump)
- `perf:` Performance improvements (patch version bump)
- `test:` Test changes (no version bump)
- `chore:` Build process or auxiliary tool changes (no version bump)
- `BREAKING CHANGE:` or `!` after type (major version bump)

Examples:
```
feat: add voice agent v3 support
fix: resolve timeout issue in call controller
feat!: redesign agent manager API
```

### Automated Release Process

The project uses a pull request-based release workflow:

1. **Automatic PR Creation**: When commits are pushed to `main`, the workflow automatically:
   - Analyzes commits to determine the next version
   - Creates a release branch (`release/vX.Y.Z`)
   - Updates version in `pyproject.toml`
   - Updates `CHANGELOG.md` with changes
   - Opens a PR with the `release` label

2. **Review and Merge**: Team reviews the release PR and merges when ready

3. **Automatic Tagging**: Upon merging a release PR, the workflow automatically:
   - Creates a git tag `vX.Y.Z`
   - Creates a GitHub release with changelog
   - Deletes the release branch
   - Triggers Docker image builds (if configured)

### Manual Release Process

For manual releases or testing:

```bash
# Check what version will be released (dry run)
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create a new version locally (updates version, creates changelog)
uv run semantic-release version --commit --no-tag --no-push

# Create release branch and push
git checkout -b release/vX.Y.Z
git push origin release/vX.Y.Z

# Create PR manually via GitHub UI or CLI
gh pr create --base main --label "release" --title "chore(release): vX.Y.Z"
```

### Release Workflow Features

- **Automatic Version Detection**: Uses conventional commits to determine version bumps
- **PR-Based Releases**: All releases go through PR review for safety
- **Automatic Cleanup**: Old release PRs are closed, branches are deleted after merge
- **GitHub Releases**: Automatic creation with extracted changelog notes
- **Protected Main Branch**: Compatible with branch protection rules
- **No Manual Tagging**: Tags are created automatically to prevent errors

### Automated Release Process

The project uses a pull request-based release workflow:

1. **Automatic PR Creation**: When commits are pushed to `main`, the workflow automatically:
   - Analyzes commits to determine the next version
   - Creates a release branch (`release/vX.Y.Z`)
   - Updates version in `pyproject.toml`
   - Updates `CHANGELOG.md` with changes
   - Opens a PR with the `release` label

2. **Review and Merge**: Team reviews the release PR and merges when ready

3. **Automatic Tagging**: Upon merging a release PR, the workflow automatically:
   - Creates a git tag `vX.Y.Z`
   - Creates a GitHub release with changelog
   - Deletes the release branch
   - Triggers Docker image builds (if configured)

### Manual Release Process

For manual releases or testing:

```bash
# Check what version will be released (dry run)
uv run semantic-release version --print

# Create a new version locally (updates version, creates changelog)
uv run semantic-release version --commit --no-tag --no-push

# Create release branch and push
git checkout -b release/vX.Y.Z
git push origin release/vX.Y.Z

# Create PR manually via GitHub UI or CLI
gh pr create --base main --label "release" --title "chore(release): vX.Y.Z"
```

### Release Workflow Features

- **Automatic Version Detection**: Uses conventional commits to determine version bumps
- **PR-Based Releases**: All releases go through PR review for safety
- **Automatic Cleanup**: Old release PRs are closed, branches are deleted after merge
- **GitHub Releases**: Automatic creation with extracted changelog notes
- **Protected Main Branch**: Compatible with branch protection rules
- **No Manual Tagging**: Tags are created automatically to prevent errors
